Sample Name: Unintentional Weight Loss and Dental Pain
Description: Evaluation of substantial weight loss with tooth and head pain, insomnia, and neuropathic complaints.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS: The patient returns with a number of concerns, including headache, earache, and pain associated with a wisdom tooth scheduled for extraction. He has noticed difficulty with vision in the left eye and reports neuropathic symptoms of the feet, for which electrodiagnostic testing is already planned by neurology. He reports approximately 30 pounds of unintentional weight loss since April, now weighing about 150 pounds at home, without a clear explanation. He denies persistent cough and overt gastrointestinal bleeding but declines colonoscopy despite counseling. He has continued tobacco use and difficulty sleeping, obtaining only several hours of sleep. Family stressors have also been substantial. Medication use was reviewed, including past amitriptyline and analgesics. He reports that ibuprofen has not helped adequately.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION: Examination of the head, neck, and lungs was undertaken, including assessment of a possible localized cervical lymph node near the symptomatic tooth.
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN:
1. Significant unexplained weight loss. Order laboratory evaluation and CT imaging of the chest and neck without intravenous contrast. Colonoscopy was recommended and discussed, but the patient is unwilling at this time. Additional investigation will depend on results.
2. Dental pain with headache and earache. Wisdom tooth removal is already scheduled. Symptomatic treatment was discussed; avoid further ibuprofen as advised by the clinician.
3. Insomnia. A trial of temazepam was proposed.
4. Neuropathic foot complaints. Keep the scheduled neurology testing appointment.
5. Additional symptoms and medication requests were reviewed, including sexual function and analgesic treatment.
The clinician will communicate test results. Routine followup in six months, earlier if the evaluation warrants it.
